title: NPPF Student Photojournalism Scholarships
summary: A common application for eleven scholarships supporting college photojournalists, visual storytellers and television news photographers.
eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate students attending a four-year U.S. college or university; international students residing in the United States are eligible.

title: JEA Journalist of the Year Scholarships
award: $4,000 top award; up to five $1,200 finalist awards
summary: National scholarships recognizing outstanding high-school journalists through reporting, writing, editing, broadcast, photojournalism and digital portfolios.
eligibility: High-school seniors who win or are selected through their state Journalist of the Year competition and whose advisers are current JEA members.

title: Future Journalism Teacher Scholarships
summary: Scholarships encouraging future educators who intend to teach scholastic journalism.
eligibility: College juniors, seniors or graduate students preparing to teach scholastic journalism who meet the current program requirements.

title: SPJ/JEA High School Essay Contest
provider: Society of Professional Journalists and Journalism Education Association
award: $1,000 first place; $500 second place; $300 third place
summary: Annual essay competition encouraging high-school students to examine journalism and press-freedom issues.
eligibility: Students enrolled in grades 9–12 at U.S. public, private or home schools who meet the current contest rules.

title: Dow Jones News Fund College Internship Program
summary: Paid summer journalism internships with specialized training and a scholarship for students who complete the program successfully.
eligibility: Eligible college juniors, seniors, graduate students and recent graduates pursuing careers in journalism; requirements vary by internship track.

title: IRE Diversity Fellowships
award: Conference registration, membership, lodging and travel assistance
summary: Training and conference assistance intended to increase representation within investigative and data journalism.
eligibility: Journalists, educators and students of color, LGBTQ+ applicants and applicants with disabilities who meet the current conference requirements.

title: Gary Marx Scholarship
award: Membership, conference registration, lodging and travel stipend
summary: Professional-development scholarship helping college journalism students and early-career journalists attend an IRE conference.
eligibility: U.S. college journalism students and journalists within five years of college graduation; preference is given to applicants from Illinois.

title: Jennifer Leonard Scholarship
award: Membership, conference registration, lodging and travel stipend
summary: Conference scholarship supporting women of modest means who are entering investigative journalism.
eligibility: Women of modest means who are college journalism students or within three years of college graduation; women of color and trans women are encouraged to apply.

title: James Richard Bennett Scholarship
award: Assistance to attend an IRE or NICAR conference
summary: Conference and training support for journalism students in four south-central states.
eligibility: Journalism students in Arkansas, Mississippi, Oklahoma or Louisiana; University of Arkansas–Fayetteville students are excluded under the current rules.

title: Chauncey Bailey Journalist of Color Investigative Reporting Fellowship
award: Yearlong training, conference support, mentorship and data services
summary: A yearlong fellowship helping a journalist of color strengthen investigative skills and complete a community-focused reporting project.
eligibility: Journalists of color interested in investigative reporting who meet the fellowship's current professional and project requirements.

title: Emma Bowen Fellows Program
award: Multi-year paid summer internships, mentorship and professional development
summary: Multi-year paid fellowships placing students with leading media, entertainment and technology companies in business, content and innovation tracks.
eligibility: Eligible college students interested in media, entertainment or technology who meet the program's age, enrollment and U.S. work-authorization requirements.

title: WIF Fellowships
award: Mentorship, career support and industry access; benefits vary
summary: Competitive fellowships for women working toward careers in film, television and screen media across creative, production, crew and business roles.
eligibility: Experience requirements vary by discipline; applicants generally need a completed work sample or qualifying professional experience.
